Because the San Joaquin Valley is crucial for the western monarch butterfly during migration the maintenance and restoration of habitat that occurs within public lands in this area is essential to prevent further decline and further need for conservation. The San Joaquin Valley contains vital habitats rich in milkweed and a variety of other nectar plants, which are critical for monarch breeding and migration. Understanding of how butterflies and other pollinators use National Wildlife Refuges (NWRs) in the area is needed to determine the role that public lands can play in reducing butterfly decline. Enhancing nectar availability is a key strategy for pollinator conservation and will benefit not just the western monarch but also other pollinator species. Restoring and improving nectar availability in native habitats can help support a variety of pollinator species. To prioritize management actions and improve conservation outcomes, it is necessary to assess the quantity and quality of existing habitats and understand how they are used by monarchs and other pollinators. Gallup Indian Medical Center (GIMC), Navajo Area IHS, provides inpatient, outpatient, emergency, critical care, surgical, women’s health, pediatric, and newborn services. Respiratory Therapy is an essential clinical service supporting patients across the lifespan. GIMC requires reliable contract staffing support to maintain continuity of respiratory care and safe hospital operations when permanent staffing is insufficient to meet operational needs. 1.2 Scope of Work The primary scope of this contract is professional Respiratory Therapy staffing services. The Contractor shall recruit, credential, clear, schedule, supervise, and provide qualified Registered Respiratory Therapists (RRTs) to fill required coverage positio ns at GIMC throughout the period of performance. The Contractor’s core organizational obligation is to ensure fully qualified, credentialed, cleared, and clinically competent personnel are available for required shifts.

Kui hankemenetlusest kõrvaldamise alus esineb, võib ettevõtja soovi korral esitada tõendeid selle kohta, et ta on võtnud meetmeid oma usaldusväärsuse taastamiseks. The contractor will deliver and refill the primary and reserve liquid oxygen tanks with 99.00% pure liquid oxygen and provide certification upon request. The Perry Point VA Medical Center is seeking to establish a base plus four option year contract with a well-qualified firm to provide medical grade liquid bulk oxygen as described herein. Perry Point requires the rental of two (2) 3,000 Gallon Medical Grade Liquid Oxygen Tank and two (2) 525 Gallon backup tank as well as the supply of medical grade liquid bulk oxygen. Each building 23H and 14H require a main tank and reserve tank at the Perry Point VA Medical Center. The Government facility does not own their own bulk oxygen tank systems, the contractor shall provide a contractor-owed tank system with an appropriate backup sys

all their bulk oxygen tank, there is a ninety-day (90) transition period at the beginning and end of the contract period. All services and equipment must comply with the latest editions of NFPA 55, Compressed Gases and Cryogenic Fluids Code and NFPA 99, Health Care Facilities Code, as well as all The Joint Commission requirements. The quantities shown in the Schedule of Supplies and Services are estimates of the VAMHCS’s annual requirements. There is no express or implied guarantee that these quantities will be purchased. The base contract period under this solicitation will be determined by completion of installation of equipment, approved certification of use and initial change to permanent system from temporary systems. The contract awarded under this solicitation will include a base pricing period plus (4) four (1) one-year pricing periods. DELIVERY SCHEDULE AND HOURS OF OPERATION: The contractor will manage the delivery in a safe manor according to Department of Transportation hazardous regulations. The contractor will utilize the 24/7 automatic alarm to monitor the overall health and function of the system, to include for management for automatic delivery (refill) of liquid oxygen. Primary liquid oxygen tanks will be refilled when automatic alarm reaches 40% and will refill the rese

ior to a weather event (Hurricane, Nor’easter, Tropical Storms, Blizzards, etc.). In the event of wildfire with forced evacuation of VHA Perry Point Facilities, the contractor will contact and coordinate with VA Perry Point Fire Department for hazard mitigation. SAFETY: The VHA Maryland Department of Engineering, VHA Maryland Supply Chain, and VA Perry Point Fire Department will require continual access to the restricted area for monitoring and emergency purposes. VHA Maryland Dept. of Engineering will be notified via email and telephone prior to routine maintenance, as-needed de-icing, emergency alarm outside of low volume, and inspection/certifications. Perry Point VA Facility is a long-term care campus with short-term behavioral and rehabilitation facilities. Drivers will remain vigilant while on campus to pedestrians and wildlife. Prior to first filling and annually thereafter, contractor must perform in-service training to all VA staff at the site and will include the following facets for contractor owned Medical Grade Bulk O2 systems: the refill procedure, any preventive maintenance support requirements that may be needed from the medical center systems, and an explanation of all the volume alarm and low pressure set points.
